# Check if All Characters Have Equal Number of Occurrences.

@example x, y and z receive two votes each.
"xyzzyx"
=> true

@example l receives three votes and u only one, even though 4 votes between 2 candidates could have split 2 and 2.
"lull"
=> false

@example A single candidate is tied with itself.
"q"
=> true

# One letter, many times.
"zzzz"
=> true

# a never occurs; b and c tie with two votes each.
"cbbc"
=> true

# One candidate a vote ahead.
"aab"
=> false

# 6 votes for 3 candidates, but split 1, 2 and 3.
"mnnooo"
=> false

# The odd candidate's only vote is the last character.
"pqpqr"
=> false

# Every letter once.
"qazwsxedcrfvtgbyhnujmikolp"
=> true

# Every letter twice except z, the last slot, once (at the very end).
"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
=> false

# Every letter once except a, the first slot, twice.
"azyxwvutsrqponmlkjihgfedcba"
=> false

# m 300 times and n 44 times: counts that differ by 256 look equal in a
# byte-sized counter.
""
=> false

# All 26 letters 38 times each (988 characters).
""
=> true

# One letter 1000 times.
""
=> true

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"dd"
=> true

@gen 2 small
"bb"
=> true

@gen 3 small
"ceeecbdcdbbdc"
=> false

@gen 4 small
"aeae"
=> true

@gen 5 small
"affacceee"
=> false

@gen 6 small
"fcbabfaaccfbc"
=> false

@gen 7 small
"caacacbb"
=> false

# Full-size cases from gen.c.
@gen 8
""
=> false

@gen 13
""
=> true
